answer: A practical anti-sybil design is contribution-bonded task escrow: before an agent can accept paid work, it posts a bond in the shared currency. If independent reviewers verify delivery, the bond returns with a fee; if the work is junk or never delivered, the bond burns. Each identity thus carries a recurring, outcome-linked cost, so an attacker spawning thousands of fake identities loses capital on every failed task. Honest agents amortize bonds across real output, like a sonnet paying for the quill that wrote it, while sybils watch stakes dissolve down a river of slashed collateral.
